item.title: Hubble and Roman Team Up on Gravitational Lenses
item.description: Gravitational lenses offer some of the best tools for studying dark matter and galactic evolution across cosmic time. Combining Hubble's archival sharpness with the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope gives astronomers an incredible multi-mission observational pipeline.
item.content:encoded:
from the cosmic magnifying-glass dept.

Gravitational lenses offer some of the best tools for studying dark matter and galactic evolution across cosmic time. Combining Hubble's archival sharpness with the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope gives astronomers an incredible multi-mission observational pipeline.

A new gallery of strong gravitational lenses captured by the Hubble Space Telescope highlights targets that will be revisited by the newly launched Roman Space Telescope. These cosmic magnifying glasses help scientists investigate dark matter distribution and the evolution of distant galaxies.

Read it · Astronomy and Space · NASA News

item.title: Saturn Hidden Behind the Lunar Limb
item.description: Occultations provide a rare dynamic moment when observing the outer planets against familiar lunar features. This image captures the quiet precision of planetary tracking and amateur-professional astrophotography at its best.
item.content:encoded:
from the planetary peekaboo dept.

Occultations provide a rare dynamic moment when observing the outer planets against familiar lunar features. This image captures the quiet precision of planetary tracking and amateur-professional astrophotography at its best.

A stunning astrophotography shot captures Saturn disappearing behind the lit limb of Earth's Moon during an occultation event. Such alignments offer a rare perspective on the relative motion of bodies in our inner and outer solar system.

Read it · Astrophotography · NASA Astronomy Picture of the Day

item.title: Modernizing .NET Apps for Windows Arm64 with GitHub Copilot
item.description: Moving legacy enterprise workloads to Arm architecture usually involves tracking down hundreds of hidden dependency blockers and build settings. Using an AI assistant to plan and execute that migration saves developers countless hours of manual audit work.
item.content:encoded:
from the silicon-migration dept.

Moving legacy enterprise workloads to Arm architecture usually involves tracking down hundreds of hidden dependency blockers and build settings. Using an AI assistant to plan and execute that migration saves developers countless hours of manual audit work.

The GitHub Copilot upgrade agent now helps developers assess and modernize existing .NET applications for migration to Windows Arm64. The tool identifies platform blockers, builds a migration plan, and updates code and configuration dependencies automatically.

Read it · DotNet and Development · Microsoft .NET Blog

item.title: Tiny Solar-Powered Transmitters Track Monarch Butterfly Migration
item.description: Weighing in at just 60 milligrams with zero batteries, these custom Bluetooth tags represent an astonishing feat of biological telemetry. It is a brilliant hardware hack connecting tiny garden visitors to modern mobile location services.
item.content:encoded:
from the lepidopteran telemetry dept.

Weighing in at just 60 milligrams with zero batteries, these custom Bluetooth tags represent an astonishing feat of biological telemetry. It is a brilliant hardware hack connecting tiny garden visitors to modern mobile location services.

Researchers are using a 60-milligram solar-powered Bluetooth transmitter attached with eyelash glue to track the incredible migration of monarch butterflies. The featherlight tags allow scientists and citizen scientists alike to follow the insects using standard smartphone location services.

Read it · DotNet and Development · Hackaday

item.title: Porting Elite to the Commodore PET
item.description: Porting a legendary open-world game to a machine with strictly block graphics four decades later is pure hacker joy. It showcases a deep appreciation for classical 6502 assembly constraints and retro systems.
item.content:encoded:
from the vintage retrocomputing dept.

Porting a legendary open-world game to a machine with strictly block graphics four decades later is pure hacker joy. It showcases a deep appreciation for classical 6502 assembly constraints and retro systems.

Developer David Given has successfully ported the iconic 1980s open-world space trading game Elite to the Commodore PET. Running on a 6502 processor with 32k of memory, the port relies on the PET's block graphics rather than modern high-resolution displays.

Read it · DotNet and Development · Hackaday

item.title: NGC 4449: The Small Galaxy Punching Above Its Weight
item.description: Dwarf galaxies often harbor intense starburst activity that rivals much larger spirals, providing crucial laboratories for stellar formation. This NASA Astronomy Picture of the Day highlights the surprising ferocity of small cosmic systems.
item.content:encoded:
from the stellar nursery dept.

Dwarf galaxies often harbor intense starburst activity that rivals much larger spirals, providing crucial laboratories for stellar formation. This NASA Astronomy Picture of the Day highlights the surprising ferocity of small cosmic systems.

A detailed look at the dwarf irregular galaxy NGC 4449 reveals a widespread, frantic wave of active star formation. Despite being a fraction of the size of the Milky Way, this small galaxy is currently manufacturing stars at an astonishing rate.

Read it · Astronomy and Space · NASA News

item.title: Chandra Unmasks a Supernova Impostor
item.description: Distinguishing between cataclysmic stellar deaths and recurring outbursts from unstable massive stars is notoriously difficult. Finding a compact binary companion behind the outbursts solves a long-standing astronomical mystery.
item.content:encoded:
from the cosmic masquerade dept.

Distinguishing between cataclysmic stellar deaths and recurring outbursts from unstable massive stars is notoriously difficult. Finding a compact binary companion behind the outbursts solves a long-standing astronomical mystery.

New research using the Chandra X-Ray Observatory reveals that a periodic 'supernova impostor' star outburst is actually powered by a binary relationship with a black hole or neutron star. Luminous Blue Variables often mimic true supernovae, but their recurring flares point to complex stellar interactions.

Read it · Astronomy and Space · Universe Today

item.title: What Happens When Asteroid Mining Hits the Market?
item.description: Discussions of space mining usually focus on the rocketry and engineering rather than the macroeconomic reality. Applying system dynamics to platinum market shocks provides a grounded look at future space industry economics.
item.content:encoded:
from the extraterrestrial commodities dept.

Discussions of space mining usually focus on the rocketry and engineering rather than the macroeconomic reality. Applying system dynamics to platinum market shocks provides a grounded look at future space industry economics.

A pair of system dynamicists from MIT have modeled the economic impact of harvesting platinum-group metals from asteroids using spacecraft like AstroForge. Their research suggests that while asteroid mining would crash rare-earth commodity prices, the broader industrial availability would benefit Earth immensely.

Read it · Astronomy and Space · Universe Today

item.title: The Ice Giants' Strange and Shifting Magnetic Fields
item.description: Uranus and Neptune have long puzzled astronomers with magnetic fields that bear little resemblance to Earth's orderly dipole. New modeling suggests these chaotic fields may change on surprisingly short timescales compared to our last visit from Voyager 2. It is a fascinating look at the dynamic interiors of the solar system's ice giants.
item.content:encoded:
from the planetary dynamo dept.

Uranus and Neptune have long puzzled astronomers with magnetic fields that bear little resemblance to Earth's orderly dipole. New modeling suggests these chaotic fields may change on surprisingly short timescales compared to our last visit from Voyager 2. It is a fascinating look at the dynamic interiors of the solar system's ice giants.

New research suggests that the messy, tilted magnetic fields of Uranus and Neptune may change on very short timescales, potentially looking quite different than they did during Voyager 2's flybys in the 1980s. These findings highlight how little we still know about the unique interiors of our solar system's ice giants.

Read it · Astronomy and Space · Universe Today

item.title: Seestar S30 Plus Review: A New Entry-Level Smart Telescope
item.description: Smart telescopes are rapidly transforming how backyard astronomers capture deep-sky objects without spending a fortune. This review of the Seestar S30 Plus offers a realistic look at what an affordable, app-controlled 30mm apochromatic setup can achieve for beginners.
item.content:encoded:
from the automated aperture dept.

Smart telescopes are rapidly transforming how backyard astronomers capture deep-sky objects without spending a fortune. This review of the Seestar S30 Plus offers a realistic look at what an affordable, app-controlled 30mm apochromatic setup can achieve for beginners.

The Seestar S30 Plus bridges the gap between ultra-portable smart scopes and traditional astrophotography gear with a $499 price tag. Featuring a 30mm aperture and dual cameras, it gives beginners an accessible way to image deep-sky targets from the backyard.

Read it · Astrophotography · AstroBackyard

item.title: Data Shows Used EV Batteries Are Holding Up Better Than Expected
item.description: Skepticism around battery longevity has been a persistent talking point for electric vehicles, but empirical data tells a much more encouraging story. Diagnostic testing from hundreds of thousands of real-world vehicles provides valuable insight into actual degradation rates over time.
item.content:encoded:
from the state-of-charge dept.

Skepticism around battery longevity has been a persistent talking point for electric vehicles, but empirical data tells a much more encouraging story. Diagnostic testing from hundreds of thousands of real-world vehicles provides valuable insight into actual degradation rates over time.

Analysis of more than 500,000 battery tests across popular electric vehicle models reveals that packs are degrading far more slowly than critics anticipated. Diagnostics companies utilizing rapid OBD tests are finding that used EV batteries retain health much better than feared.

Read it · DotNet and Development · Hackaday

item.title: Modular, 3D-Printed Train Whistles for Your Inner Conductor
item.description: There is something inherently delightful about well-engineered mechanical projects that serve a purely whimsical purpose. This 3D-printable, modular train whistle lets makers swap resonant chambers on the fly to replicate historic steam whistle chimes.
item.content:encoded:
from the resonant chamber dept.

There is something inherently delightful about well-engineered mechanical projects that serve a purely whimsical purpose. This 3D-printable, modular train whistle lets makers swap resonant chambers on the fly to replicate historic steam whistle chimes.

A clever 3D-printing project offers a modular 3-inch train whistle with adjustable bell caps to change resonant notes on the fly. By tweaking the chamber dimensions, makers can switch between authentic historic steam whistle chimes using common FDM printers.

Read it · DotNet and Development · Hackaday

item.title: The Invisible Lamplighter of The Hague
item.description: Hidden urban art pieces that celebrate forgotten historical professions are always worth highlighting. This charming bronze sculpture in The Hague captures a lamplighter mid-climb from an era before automated electricity took over.
item.content:encoded:
from the bronze age dept.

Hidden urban art pieces that celebrate forgotten historical professions are always worth highlighting. This charming bronze sculpture in The Hague captures a lamplighter mid-climb from an era before automated electricity took over.

Tucked away in an alleyway in The Hague, a bronze sculpture titled De Lantaarnopsteker depicts a lamplighter scrambling up a lamp post. Created by Dutch sculptor Loek Bos, the artwork immortalizes the historic trade of manually lighting city streets before automated electricity.

Read it · Curious Discoveries · Atlas Obscura

item.title: MEUTE: The 11-Piece Techno Marching Band
item.description: Bridging the gap between electronic club music and traditional marching band instrumentation is a wonderfully eccentric creative pursuit. It is a refreshing antidote to algorithmic monotony.
item.content:encoded:
from the acoustic bassline dept.

Bridging the gap between electronic club music and traditional marching band instrumentation is a wonderfully eccentric creative pursuit. It is a refreshing antidote to algorithmic monotony.

MEUTE is an 11-piece German marching band that swaps synthesizers and laptops for tubas, trombones, and drum kits to perform electronic music acoustically. Their unique arrangements bring a surprisingly rich physical energy to modern techno tracks.

Read it · Wildcard · Kottke

item.title: Hot Jupiter Vanishes from Sight After Gravitational Tug from Unseen Neighbor
item.description: When a transiting exoplanet monitored by TESS for seven years suddenly stops showing up, it forces astronomers to look closer at orbital dynamics. This clear, source-backed finding explains how a neighboring giant planet can gravitationally tug a world right out of our line of sight.
item.content:encoded:
from the disappearing-act dept.

When a transiting exoplanet monitored by TESS for seven years suddenly stops showing up, it forces astronomers to look closer at orbital dynamics. This clear, source-backed finding explains how a neighboring giant planet can gravitationally tug a world right out of our line of sight.

Astronomers analyzing seven years of TESS data discovered that a hot Jupiter about 1,000 light-years away stopped transiting its star. They determined that an unseen massive companion planet gravitationally tugged the world off its previous transit alignment.

Read it · Astronomy and Space · Universe Today

item.title: This Smart Coffee Kiosk Is Now Playing DOOM
item.description: There is a wonderful, enduring hacker tradition of getting id Software's classic shooter running on anything with a microprocessor. This detailed teardown of a Linux-powered commercial coffee kiosk provides a clever look into embedded hacking and low-level debugging ports.
item.content:encoded:
from the caffeine-and-frag-grenades dept.

There is a wonderful, enduring hacker tradition of getting id Software's classic shooter running on anything with a microprocessor. This detailed teardown of a Linux-powered commercial coffee kiosk provides a clever look into embedded hacking and low-level debugging ports.

A hardware hacker managed to run DOOM on the i.MX 6 ARM Cortex-A9 processor powering a commercial self-serve coffee kiosk's touchscreen module. By probing the debug port on the machine's smart controller, they added a whole new kind of hard mode to your morning caffeine run.

Read it · DotNet and Development · Hackaday

item.description: With modern skies growing crowded with constellations, open-source utilities that let developers run SGP4 orbital mechanics locally in the browser are fantastic. It is a neat engineering project that highlights how everyday observers can monitor passing hardware and downlinked data.
item.content:encoded:
from the low-earth-orbit dept.

With modern skies growing crowded with constellations, open-source utilities that let developers run SGP4 orbital mechanics locally in the browser are fantastic. It is a neat engineering project that highlights how everyday observers can monitor passing hardware and downlinked data.

A developer has built a browser-based satellite tracker using simplified perturbation models to map passes over any location in real time. The open-source tool runs entirely client-side and can automatically pull imagery transmitted by passing spacecraft.

Read it · DotNet and Development · Hackaday

item.title: Voyager 1 Reaches One Light-Day Distance from Earth
item.description: Reaching a distance where radio signals take 24 hours to make a one-way trip is a mind-boggling milestone for humanity's most distant emissary. NASA's celebration of Voyager 1's historic 50-year journey offers a wonderful moment to reflect on interstellar operations.
item.content:encoded:
from the deep-space-signal dept.

Reaching a distance where radio signals take 24 hours to make a one-way trip is a mind-boggling milestone for humanity's most distant emissary. NASA's celebration of Voyager 1's historic 50-year journey offers a wonderful moment to reflect on interstellar operations.

Nearly 50 years after its launch in 1977, Voyager 1 is set to cross the one light-day distance threshold, sitting more than 16 billion miles away from Earth. NASA is marking the historic interplanetary milestone with public engagement events and global participation.

Read it · Astronomy and Space · NASA News

item.title: First Direct Measurement of Cosmic Hydrogen Mapping the Universe
item.description: Radio astronomy breakthroughs that give us a new handle on large-scale cosmic structure are always worth highlighting. The MeerKLASS collaboration's work offers a concrete look at how direct hydrogen mapping will change cosmological surveys.
item.content:encoded:
from the neutral-gas dept.

Radio astronomy breakthroughs that give us a new handle on large-scale cosmic structure are always worth highlighting. The MeerKLASS collaboration's work offers a concrete look at how direct hydrogen mapping will change cosmological surveys.

The international MeerKLASS collaboration has achieved the first direct measurement of the large-scale clustering of cosmic hydrogen in the universe. The breakthrough technique promises to open new ways for astronomers to map cosmic structure and galaxy evolution.

Read it · Astronomy and Space · Universe Today

item.title: Automated Assembly in Space Is the Future and NOM4D Is Showing the Way
item.description: Moving past pre-constructed station modules requires entirely new robotic assembly techniques for large structures in orbit. Programs like NOM4D are proving that simple automated systems can successfully build trusses from component parts.
item.content:encoded:
from the orbital construction dept.

Moving past pre-constructed station modules requires entirely new robotic assembly techniques for large structures in orbit. Programs like NOM4D are proving that simple automated systems can successfully build trusses from component parts.

A new space construction program called NOM4D demonstrated that autonomous robots can successfully assemble truss-like structures in space using premade components. This milestone marks a step forward in our ability to fabricate large infrastructure directly in orbit.

Read it · Astronomy and Space · Universe Today

item.title: NASA Scientists Show How Gravitational Waves Can Reveal New Worlds
item.description: Combining gravitational wave astronomy with exoplanet hunting opens up an entirely novel way to detect distant worlds. Upcoming observatories like LISA could soon spot planets orbiting tightly bound white dwarf systems thousands of light-years away.
item.content:encoded:
from the spacetime ripples dept.

Combining gravitational wave astronomy with exoplanet hunting opens up an entirely novel way to detect distant worlds. Upcoming observatories like LISA could soon spot planets orbiting tightly bound white dwarf systems thousands of light-years away.

Recent studies led by NASA astrophysicists detail how the upcoming LISA gravitational wave observatory could detect exoplanets throughout our galaxy. By analyzing how a planet modifies gravitational wave signals from orbiting white dwarfs, astronomers can spot unseen worlds.

Read it · Astronomy and Space · NASA News

item.title: Rigel and the Witch Head Nebula
item.description: Reflection nebulae illuminated by bright supergiants always provide stunning visual targets for astrophotographers. IC 2118 near Rigel offers a classic case of pareidolia coupled with intricate interstellar dust structures.
item.content:encoded:
from the cosmic illusion dept.

Reflection nebulae illuminated by bright supergiants always provide stunning visual targets for astrophotographers. IC 2118 near Rigel offers a classic case of pareidolia coupled with intricate interstellar dust structures.

An astrophotograph captures IC 2118, a faint reflection nebula known popularly as the Witch Head Nebula due to its uncanny resemblance to a caricature. Illuminated by the bright blue supergiant Rigel, the sprawling dust cloud spans about 50 light-years.

Read it · Astrophotography · NASA Astronomy Picture of the Day

item.title: Do AI Coding Agents Care About SemVer?
item.description: This is a clever piece of practical engineering research that tests an assumption about how autonomous agents interact with codebases. It turns out that version numbers still act as a subtle psychological nudge even for LLMs.
item.content:encoded:
from the semantic versioning dept.

This is a clever piece of practical engineering research that tests an assumption about how autonomous agents interact with codebases. It turns out that version numbers still act as a subtle psychological nudge even for LLMs.

Microsoft researchers tested whether AI coding agents pay attention to semantic versioning when upgrading dependencies. Surprisingly, experiments revealed that version numbers alone changed how models handled byte-identical code modifications.

Read it · AI and Agents · Microsoft DevBlogs
